newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi says window closing on tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi says window closing on tobacco deal.

text.p: Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said Monday tobacco companies had only a few days to settle his state's $940 million Medicaid lawsuit or a trial would begin July 9.

"I'm optimistic. I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to settle with us because I think their chances are not good in Mississippi," Moore told reporters before leaving for negotiations in Washington.

Mississippi's case is the first of 40 similar state government lawsuits to go to trial. Each seeks payment for treating sick smokers through Medicaid health care programs. Florida and Texas have cases scheduled for trial this summer.

An out-of-court agreement was reached June 20 between the tobacco industry and the state governments tentatively settling the lawsuits, but President Clinton and Congress must approve the deal. No Washington action is expected for months.

Moore, one of the most prominent figures on the anti-tobacco side in the tobacco talks, wants the tobacco defendants to guarantee Mississippi's likely 1 percent share of the $368.5 billion settlement reached June 20, even if the deal should come undone.
"If I can't get it done within a couple of days, it's not going to happen," Moore said.

The judge overseeing Moore's lawsuit, Jackson County Chancery Judge William Myers, met briefly with lawyers for both sides Monday and postponed until July 7 and 8 pretrial hearings, which had been set for Tuesday and Wednesday.
